#+title: bibelot internals
#+subtitle: the desktop widget engine
#+options: toc:nil num:nil

The cards are a separate project from the shell that hosts them.  This page is
the engine's map; the settings language and the user-facing widget gallery are
documented by the host (whelk's =docs/widgets.org=).

* The data and the cards

=src/widgets.rs= owns everything about a card that does not need a display: the
sixteen kinds and their standard sizes, position/size/monitor defaults and
clamps, the mouse vocabulary and per-kind refresh cadence, the reminders model
whose done flags are runtime state, world-clock city parsing, the
Open-Meteo/Yahoo/RSS-Atom answer decoding, the calendar's Monday-first month
grid and ISO week numbers, a note's file-or-text rule, the photo folder walk,
the recent-documents XBEL reader, the system's =/proc= readers, the stock
sparkline arithmetic and the drag/placement arithmetic.

=src/widgetstate.rs= is the =widgets-<settings-stem>.ini= file the shell writes
and reads, so a drag is remembered across restarts.  Positions are stored per
monitor with a monitor-less fallback; the file is clamped into whatever screen
is left when a connector disappears.

=src/desktopwidgets.rs= draws the cards: one bottom-layer surface per configured
widget, anchored at its saved or configured place, skinned from the host's
palette, moved by its grip, with a timer per kind and a second tick on Weather,
Stocks and News that only re-reads their age.  Networked cards make one
asynchronous request at a time; a card that goes away drops its timer, its skin
and its surface, and an answer that arrives late paints nothing.  The manager
is rebuilt when the configuration, the material or the outputs changed, and
otherwise keeps the cards it has.

* The readers

The cards do not call the shell for a reading.  =src/batterybar.rs= reads
`/sys/class/power_supply`, =src/cpubar.rs= samples `/proc/stat`,
=src/memorybar.rs= parses `/proc/meminfo`, =src/mpris.rs= watches the session
bus, =src/visualizer.rs= owns one cava process, and =src/command.rs=,
=src/json.rs=, =src/format.rs= and =src/sources.rs= are the small shared
readers behind the networked and command cards.  Each one is independent of
the shell's bar modules, even where the two read the same kernel file.

* The skin

The host supplies a =bibelot::Skin=: the first bar's palette, material options
and the frosted-glass finish in force.  =src/style.rs= turns it into one
stylesheet scoped to the card's window id; =src/widgets.rs= can overlay a
card's own skin keys on that copy, and =src/desktopwidgets.rs= adds the
transparency rules last.  The structural rules live in =CARD_CSS= and are
installed once per display; a theme change replaces them.

* The Scheme theme

=scheme/bibelot/theme.scm= exports =widget-theme=, =configure-widgets!= and
=reset-widget-theme!=.  The alist has three keys: =card-padding= and
=card-gap= in pixels, and =extra-css= for anything the structural rules do not
name.  The defaults in =src/theme.rs= and the Scheme module are kept together
by a test.

A host with its own Guile loads the module and calls =Theme::from_alist=;
=src/guile.rs= exists for a host without one.  Guile is global and
thread-affine, so only one runtime can be initialized in a process.  The theme
test therefore has its own =main= and no libtest harness.
